steps.title: Cava
steps.body: Cava is Spain's traditional method wine, about 95% from Catalonia's Penedès. Macabeo, Xarel-lo and Parellada are the main grapes; Chardonnay and Pinot Noir are allowed. The 2020 rules created zones and a top tier, Cava de Paraje Calificado, from single estates aged at least 36 months. Corpinnat producers left the DO for stricter organic rules.

steps.title: Crémant
steps.body: Crémant is France's traditional method wine outside Champagne, made in eight AOPs, including Alsace, Burgundy, Loire, Jura, Limoux and Bordeaux. Rules require whole bunch pressing, a limit on juice yield, and at least 9 months on lees. Each uses local grapes: Chenin Blanc in the Loire, Pinot Blanc and Riesling in Alsace, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir in Burgundy.
steps.highlight: Eight crémant AOPs, 9 months on lees

steps.prompt: Match each sparkling wine to its country.
steps.explanation: The traditional method is used worldwide under many names.

steps.title: Other leaders
steps.body: Franciacorta, in Lombardy, needs 18 months on lees for non-vintage and is mainly Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Trentodoc, in Trentino, is mountain-grown. England's south, on chalk similar to Champagne's, has become a serious producer. South Africa's Méthode Cap Classique and Tasmania also make fine examples.

steps.prompt: Crémant must spend at least 9 months on its lees.
steps.explanation: Yes. That's the minimum for all French crémants.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cava is mostly from Penedès, with a new single estate tier
Crémant is made in eight French AOPs with local grapes
Franciacorta, Trentodoc, England and Tasmania also excel
